recipes.name: Irish Tacos
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Mix yogurt, mayonnaise, lime juice, cilantro, cayenne pepper, and salt together in a bowl until smooth. Set aside.
Place corned beef in a saucepan over medium-low heat; cook, stirring occasionally, just until hot.
While corned beef is warming, place a tortilla into a heavy skillet over medium heat until hot and just beginning to show brown spots, about 30 seconds per side. Repeat to warm remaining tortillas.
Arrange about 2 tablespoons coleslaw in the center of each tortilla; top each with about 3 tablespoons corned beef. Drizzle each taco with 2 tablespoons yogurt sauce; roll up to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Tacos
raw_recipe.description: Irish tacos may not be what you expect when you think of tacos, but these corned beef and coleslaw tacos with cilantro-lime sauce are just delicious.

review.reviewBody: These are a favorite in my house after St. Patty's Day. I usually use corn tortillas and add mashed spuds if they are around. Top with tangy sharp shredded cheddar cheese and these are Great!! The combo of coleslaw and corned beef reminds me of NY deli sammies, OH YUMMO. Thank You PacNWCook. Got a good one here:)

Yum, Yum, Yum ~ My family and my parents really enjoyed this new twist on tacos. To save time, I cooked the corned beef in the crock-pot all day and then shredded the meat before serving. We liked the combination of the yogurt sauce and the coleslaw. This makes way more yogurt sauce than what is needed for the recipe. I easily had enough of the sauce leftover that I could have used it for the slaw dressing instead of regular slaw dressing. I am going to do that the next time I make this recipe. I also added about a teaspoon of cayenne pepper as a dash was not even noticeable. I warmed the tortillas on a griddle so that I could heat more than one at a time. This recipe is repeat worthy - and I tried it just in time to stock up on corned beef that will soon be on sale for St. Patrick's Day.

@Warren Pope: NOWHERE in the recipe does it say the corned beef is from a CAN. The recipe made with leftover corned beef (or in a pinch I might use deli corned beef) is surprisingly delicious. I used corn tortillas because I had those on hand. Yes the sauce portion makes a lot but you can put it in a squeeze bottle and use it on other things (including "regular" tacos). It keeps in the refrigerator for about a week.

I thought these were alright! Not something that I would have regularly, but once a year, absolutely. I think the sauce recipe is a bit off like there should be one less cup of greek yogurt. It made way too much sauce for the amount of tacos it made, and my sauce, by comparison to the pictures, was pure white, not even close to a green color, and tasted mostly like yogurt, very little like cilantro or lime. Not bad, but I think some small improvements would have made it better. I did like browning the flour tortillas in a pan. It made for a nice way to eat them that I had never done before.

This is my families favorite meal. I use the restaraunt style cole slaw recipe in here and have tried multiple corned beef recipes from here (haven’t found one to be that much better than another yet, all decently good). If I forget to buy plain yogurt, I’ll just use sour cream instead. I’ll also use both regular flour and corn tortillas.
VERY YUMMY! The picture looks like they added grated cheese, but I don't see that as an ingredient in the recipe.

This is pretty good 👍 Will definitely try again but won’t really shred the meat. Love the sauce and the slaw is a nice crunchy addition. I’m going to try using it with shredded chicken or sautéed shrimp.
I used this recipie for fish tacos instead and they were so delicious! The sauce added just the right touch to my tilipia and worked wonderfully with the coleslaw!!

Very good flavor combinations--a great way for our Irish family to celebrate the St. Patty's holiday, and we enjoyed them a lot. Based on other reviews, we added some mashed potatoes, which was good, but would I would have enjoyed them the same without the spuds. I wish corned beef wasn't so pricey--we would make these a lot more often.
Will make this again if I ever have leftover corned beef.

These were pretty good. I was looking for something to do with the left over moist of a brisket I smoked this past weekend, this did the trick. I used shredded moist brisket instead of corned beef and used the left over cole slaw. Applebee's has an appetizer that is Brisket Won Tons. It brisket, BBQ sauce and cooler slaw in a fried won ton wrapper like a taco shell, they're really good also for leftover brisket.

Great change for a big gathering I host for St Paddy's Day. My wife cooks the traditional Corned Beef, while I smoke one or two. I used the smoked one for this recipe. It was a huge hit. I felt the sauce was a little bland. Most of my guests like spicy but not hot. I added smoked paprika and chili powder which kept it fairly true to original recipe with a bit more spice. Just for kicks, and mostly because I am one of those guys who likes to try everything, I added all the traditional side for tacos, but made sure I told everyone what the traditional Irish Taco has on it. Most folks loved it as directed by the recipe. Many comments on how good the sauce was too.
Nice simple recipe that even my son love to make.
I followed the directions as stated and they were delicious!

This combination is outstanding this is the first time I have fixed this with the sauce, but it is also good with the corned beef and a big spoon full of prepared Cole slaw, the two ingredients compliment in taste and texture!
I can see the potential here, but the canned corned beef was a letdown. I'll try better meat next time

I am so ECSTATIC to have found this recipe, which I have been looking for for a number of years!! I had my first Corn Beef Taco in an Irish Pub, years ago in Southern California, & not only were they $1 tacos but they were the best tacos I had ever had! This recipe is almost exactly like what I tasted & determined that's what was in those very tacos. So excited to make these tomorrow, it is after all St. Patrick's Day today, I have my 2nd (in 2 days) braised corn beef (that recipe is on here as well & THE BEST corn beef I have EVER made/tasted & I will never go back to boiling my corn beef ever again! By far the best I have ever eaten & my family & friends agree it is the best they have ever had, too!) in the oven now, so I was really praying to have found THIS recipe & I DID! My family & I cannot wait to have these tomorrow!! Thank YOU for sharing this & I'm hoping (by the reviews they are!!) that they are just like the Irish Pubs in So Cal! The only change I'm going to make is, like other reviews, changing the tortilla to corn tortillas, as that's how I originally had them & I, personally prefer corn vs flour, especially with these particular tacos. Thank YOU for sharing THIS AMAZING, DELICIOUS, one of a kind recipe!! Counting down until tomorrow's supper...we might just have to have them for lunch instead, I can't wait until supper tomorrow to have these! Thank you! Thank you! I will write a review after I make these as well, so excited!! Made my St. Patty's Day!!
